market.headline: Anthropic priced its record IPO above range and Nasdaq futures are up about 2% this morning, but the Fed looks set to raise rates in December.
points: Wednesday: The S&P 500 slipped 0.2% for its fifth loss in a row and the Dow fell 1.1%, but the Nasdaq rose 0.4%. Nvidia gave back its early gains and closed down 2.9% even after strong results. AMD jumped 5.3% and Broadcom 3.6%.
Health care was the weakest group, down 2.2%. A proposed US rule to claw back Medicare Advantage overpayments sank insurers like UnitedHealth (down 10%), and drug makers like Lilly and J&J slid too.

Rates: The Fed's October notes showed almost every official thinks more rate hikes are likely. Traders now see about a 9 in 10 chance of a hike on Dec 9. The 10-year US bond yield is about 5.07%. Higher rates tend to weigh on pricey stocks.

Today: Anthropic starts trading on the Nasdaq after pricing at $83 a share, raising about $81 billion. The new US chip export rules start today, P&G holds its investor day, Walmart reports, and Trump, Xi and Putin meet in Shenzhen.
market.plan: A strong IPO morning can fade by the afternoon, like Nvidia did yesterday. Keep new buys small and stick to the calm names and halal funds until the December rate decision is clearer.

stocks.sum: The simple, certified way to own about 220 halal US companies at once.
why: About 10% below its high after a run of down days, so you are not buying at the top.
One purchase spreads your money over many companies, so one bad stock hurts less.
Certified halal, so there is no screening homework.
risk: Nvidia and Apple are a big part of the fund, so big tech news moves it a lot.
The Fed looks set to raise rates in December, which could keep the market choppy for a few weeks.
I could not confirm a close after Nov 17, so the price shown is from then. Check the live price in your app.
stocks.todo: Still the best first purchase on this list. Buy in two or three small pieces over the next couple of weeks so one bad day doesn't decide your price.

stocks.sum: A calm, Canadian-dollar halal fund. No currency fee when you buy it.
why: Trades in Canadian dollars, so you skip the 1.5% US currency fee each way.
Holds steady companies around the world and moves much less than tech.
Certified halal.
risk: Slow mover. Good for safety, weak for quick gains.
It dipped about 1.2% on Nov 17 with world markets. That is still only about 3% below its high.
stocks.todo: A sensible place for money you can't afford to see swing, like a down payment. Check the live price first and use a limit order.

stocks.n: SP Funds Dow Jones Global Sukuk ETF
stocks.sum: A halal income fund that pays monthly, about 4.9% a year. Not a growth play.
why: Pays a small amount every month.
Barely moves when stocks drop.
risk: It sits less than 1% above its 52-week low of $17.30. The Fed's notes point to more rate hikes, and funds like this tend to drift lower when rates rise.
US withholding tax takes 15% of the payouts inside an FHSA.
I could not confirm a close after Nov 17.
stocks.todo: Only use it to park cash for income. It will not help a few-month profit goal.

stocks.earnNote: Broadcom, a big holding, reports Dec 9
stocks.sum: The chip rebound trade without leverage, spread over 26 chip makers.
why: About 32% below its high, so there is real room to recover.
It held nearly flat on Wednesday while Nvidia fell, because gains in AMD and Broadcom made up for it. That is the point of owning a basket.
risk: It moves almost twice as much as the market and is down about 15% in a month.
The new US chip export rules start today, and chip futures are swinging on the Anthropic IPO.
stocks.todo: Let the chip rules and the Anthropic debut settle. If chips hold their ground into next week, think about one share.

stocks.sum: The AI chip leader. Great results, but the stock keeps falling on worries about who runs it.
why: Sales doubled from a year ago to about $116 billion, and next quarter's forecast of about $130 billion beat what analysts expected.
About 38% below its high, and cheap against its expected profits. It was up about 2% before Thursday's open.
risk: It closed down 2.9% on Wednesday after rising early, its fifth loss in a row. It sits only about 1.5% above its 52-week low.
The board says it will not bring back Jensen Huang. He faces closed-door interviews with Congress on Dec 1, and Moody's cut its credit outlook over the leadership mess.
It moves more than twice as much as the market, and the new chip export rules start today.
stocks.todo: Keep waiting. A stock that falls on good news is telling you the worry isn't over. Look again after the Dec 1 hearings or when a new CEO is named.

stocks.sum: A big winner from custom AI chips, about 28% below its high.
why: It rose 3.6% on Wednesday, one of the strongest big chip names after Nvidia's results.
Analysts' average target is well above the price.
risk: Its own earnings on Dec 9 are the next big test, about three weeks away.
Two strong days in a row can reverse fast, and the new chip rules start today.
stocks.todo: Let the chip rules kick in and the bounce cool off. If you buy, plan to be out or smaller before Dec 9.

stocks.sum: Strong business, but the wildest stock on this list.
why: Record quarter on Nov 3, and it jumped 5.3% on Wednesday after Nvidia's results.
risk: It moves two and a half times as much as the market. In the last week it fell almost 9% one day and rose 5% another.
Singapore was about 12% of its sales last year, so the new US licence rules for Southeast Asia, starting today, are a direct risk.
Very expensive against current profits, so bad news hits it hard.
stocks.todo: Skip it for now. A normal stop can't protect you well on a stock that swings this much.

stocks.sum: Makes the chips for nearly every AI company, so it wins whoever leads.
why: About 26% below its high, and it just reported a record month of sales.
It ended a four-day losing run with a 0.8% gain Wednesday and rose a bit more after hours.
risk: One up day doesn't make a trend after a long slide.
Taiwan and US-China politics are a standing risk. The new US chip rules start today, and Trump meets Xi in Shenzhen.
stocks.todo: Wait until the chip rules take effect and the price holds steady for a few days, then consider one share.

stocks.sum: The steady one in tech, but software stocks are still shaky.
why: About 9% below its high, a smaller drop than most of tech.
Moves about the same as the market, so the stop can be tighter.
It steadied Wednesday, up 0.4%, and a Microsoft exec has already explained last week's outage: a hidden bug from an earlier network fix.
risk: Software stocks were hit hard this week on fears that AI tools will replace some software.
The final outage report is due Friday. Bill Ackman's fund also cut its Microsoft stake, though he says he still likes it.
One share is about $720 CAD, a big piece of a small account.
stocks.todo: Still wait. Let Friday's outage report pass. If it steadies next week, a limit order for one share is fair.

stocks.sum: The cheapest big tech name against its profits, about 31% below its high.
why: Its price-to-earnings is near 15, which is low for a big tech company. That means you pay less for each dollar of profit.
Its income comes from ads and cloud, so it depends less on chip spending.
It owns a big stake in Anthropic. It rose 0.8% on Wednesday and about 4% before Thursday's open after the IPO priced above range.
risk: A premarket jump can fade once trading starts. If Anthropic's debut disappoints, Alphabet could give it all back.
Investors still worry about how much it is spending on AI.
It sits only about 4% above its 52-week low. Cheap stocks can get cheaper.
stocks.todo: Let today's Anthropic debut play out. If Alphabet holds its gains for a few days, look at buying one share.

stocks.sum: A safe haven lately, but priced at the top.
why: Investors have moved into Apple while chips fell. It edged up 0.2% on Wednesday.
risk: It sits about 2% below its all-time high and above analysts' average target.
Pricey against profits, so there is little room left for a few-month trade.
stocks.todo: Hold off. Put it on your list for a pullback of 8% or more.

stocks.sum: A story stock. The price runs on headlines more than on profits.
why: About 23% below its high, it rose about 1% Wednesday, and Elon Musk outlined plans to boost production in Shanghai.
risk: Extremely expensive against its profits.
It swings on headlines like robotaxi news, a possible SpaceX tie-up and China sales, more than on actual profits.
stocks.todo: Skip for a planned, rule-based trade. Too unpredictable.

stocks.sum: Reasonably priced and about 21% below its high, but the halal status needs your own check.
why: Fair price against profits, and analysts' target is well above today's price.
risk: Halal screeners do not all agree on Meta. Check Zoya or Musaffa first.
It slipped 0.4% on Wednesday and is borrowing heavily to pay for AI.
The Anthropic IPO today could shift money around in big tech.
stocks.todo: Settle the halal question first. If it passes for you, look again once the Anthropic debut settles.

stocks.sum: The weight-loss drug leader, about 5% below a record high.
why: Not a tech stock, so it spreads your risk.
It usually moves much less than the market.
risk: It fell 2.3% on Wednesday as health stocks sold off over a new US Medicare audit plan. That fight could drag on until comments close in January.
Still expensive against profits and close to analysts' average target.
One share costs about $1,960 CAD.
stocks.todo: Hold off. Too big for one share on a $10,000 account, and the dip is small so far.

stocks.sum: A defensive stock that investors ran to during the tech selloff.
why: Very calm. It usually hardly reacts to market drops.
risk: It fell 2.2% on Wednesday with other health stocks, but it is still near analysts' average target, so there is little room left.
The talc lawsuits are still ongoing.
stocks.todo: Hold off. Good company, but you would still be buying near the top of its run.

stocks.sum: A calm health care name about 21% below its high. It held up well on a rough day.
why: It slipped only 0.3% on Wednesday while health care as a group fell 2.2%.
A discount without tech's wild swings, and steady product news.
A low share price means you can buy several shares and size the trade exactly.
risk: The US Medicare audit plan is weighing on the whole health group, and that news is not settled.
Health stocks can stay out of favour for a long time.
stocks.todo: Still wait, but it is close. If it keeps holding steady for a few more days while health stocks settle, buying in one go would be fair.

stocks.sum: Soap, diapers and razors. Steady, but near its high.
why: People buy its products in any economy, and it just raised its dividend for the 70th year in a row.
risk: It closed at about $171.72 on Nov 17, less than 1% below its high. I could not confirm Wednesday's close.
Its investor day is today. New targets or plans can move the price either way.
stocks.todo: Hold off. Useful as a safe corner later, not as a profit trade now.

stocks.halalNote: Typically passes Shariah screens. Check before buying
stocks.sum: Beat forecasts this week and named a new CEO, but the stock keeps drifting lower.
why: Sales and profit came in a little above forecasts, and it kept its full-year plan.
Fair price against profits, and older US homes need repairs.
risk: It slipped another 0.4% Wednesday. Lowe's also beat forecasts, but part of its profit came from one-time tariff refunds.
The finance chief, Richard McPhail, takes over as CEO on Nov 23. Leadership changes can bring new plans and surprises.
High rates slow home sales and big renovations, and the Fed is leaning toward a December hike.
stocks.todo: Let the new CEO start and the price stop sliding before buying.

stocks.sum: Sells gases that factories and hospitals need every day. Quiet and steady.
why: About 7% below its high and calmer than the market.
It has raised its dividend for decades, which signals a stable business.
Nothing to do with the AI trade, so it spreads your risk.
risk: It slipped 0.6% on Wednesday with materials stocks, so it is not immune to selloffs.
One share is about $725 CAD, and the gap to analysts' target is small, so expect slow gains.
stocks.todo: A fair buy for one share if you want something outside tech. Use a limit order a little under the last price.
